items.q: How hot can a PP loop be sanitized?
items.a: Natural polypropylene (PP) is rated 0 to 80 °C, and its pressure rating falls as it heats. Any hot-water cycle stays inside the PP maker's pressure–temperature curve for its hours: [maximum loop sanitization temperature for PP, °C]. Routine 80 °C at loop pressure, a hot-held loop or steam needs a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) or stainless loop [whether we quote PVDF].
L runs from the main pipe's inside wall to the valve seal point; D is the branch's inside diameter. We measure every tee and sample valve and list each in the dead leg register.

items.q: How do you keep flow turbulent when several outlets open?
items.a: We size pipe and pump for the worst-case outlet combination, not the average. At the site acceptance test (SAT), we open those outlets together and record return flow.

items.q: Can we add points of use later?
items.a: Yes, after a hydraulic check at the new peak demand. Each branch is cut in with [PP point-of-use valve type] under your change control. Shutdown: [typical shutdown for a point-of-use addition, days].
